blocks.text: Rasulullaah ﷺ then accepted her pledge of allegiance in conformance with the verse of the Qur'aan.[^1]
Hadhrat Azza bint Khaabil (RA) pledges Allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ

Hadhrat Azza bint Khaabil (RA) approached Rasulullaah ﷺ and pledged that she would not fornicate, would not steal and would not bury her children alive neither in public nor in secrecy. Hadhrat Azza (RA) says, "I knew well what Rasulullaah ﷺ meant by publicly burying children alive but I did not ask Rasulullaah ﷺ what burying them alive in secrecy meant, neither did he inform me. However, it occurred to me that it refers to spoiling children. By Allaah! I shall never spoil any child of mine."[^2]
Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba (RA) Pledges Allegiance Along with her Sister Hadhrat Hind (RA) who was the Wife of Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA)

Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba bin Rabee'ah bin Abdish Shams (RA) narrates that Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfa bin Utba (RA) took her along with (her sister) Hadhrat Hind bint Utba (RA) to Rasulullaah ﷺ so that they could pledge their allegiance to him. Rasulullaah ﷺ took their promises and made some conditions with them. Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba (RA) they asked Rasulullaah ﷺ, "O my cousin! Have you noticed any of these evils or deficiencies in your people?" Hadhrat Abu Hudhayfa (RA) said, "Be quiet and make your pledge! It is with these words and conditions that the pledge of allegiance is made.

Hadhrat Hind (RA) then said, "I shall not pledge to abstain from stealing because I steal from my husband." At this, both she and Rasulullaah ﷺ held back until Rasulullaah ﷺ sent someone to (her husband) Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) to get him to permit her (to take from his possessions without seeking permission). Hadhrat Abu Sufyaan (RA) permitted her to take from the wet things (referring to foodstuffs) but did not permit her to take from the dry things (referring to non-food items such as money and clothing) or from luxuries.

The two ladies then pledged allegiance to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Hadhrat Faatima bint Utba (RA) then said to Rasulullaah ﷺ, "There was not a tent that I hated more than your tent and I wished that Allaah would destroy it and everything in it. However, I now wish more for your tent than any other that Allaah should make it prosperous and full of blessings. Rasulullaah ﷺ commented, "This ought to be because I swear by Allaah that none of you can have true Imaan until I am more beloved to him than even his children and parents."[^3]
